title: VTTI/VDOT thermal-camera AI wildlife detection pilot on Route 460 near Grundy, Virginia: 97% detection accuracy and a 3 mph average speed drop at activated signs
summary: One-year VTTI pilot for VDOT on Route 460 near Grundy: AI on thermal feeds triggered warning signs; 97% detection accuracy, 3 mph average slowdown; collisions prevented not established.
account: Bioengineer.org reported on 20 October 2026, reproducing a Virginia Tech Transportation Institute (VTTI) release, on a one-year pilot that ended in September 2026. It ran on Route 460 near Grundy in Southwest Virginia, sponsored by the Virginia Department of Transportation (VDOT) as part of the Corridor Q expansion. Eight portable solar-powered trailers with thermal cameras were installed on a 750-meter section of a 14-mile corridor that is home to about 100 elk. AI software from Crosstek analyzed the camera feeds. When wildlife was detected, dynamic message signs told motorists that wildlife had been detected ahead and to slow down. T-Mobile provided 5G and satellite links. The system achieved 97 percent overall accuracy in identifying medium and large wildlife. The initial analysis found an average speed reduction of 3 mph as vehicles approached activated signs. The report states the study did not directly establish whether the system prevented collisions or fatalities. WCYB had reported the test on 19 November 2025. It quoted VDOT that the system identifies a large animal on the road and communicates with the message boards. No peer-reviewed paper or VDOT document is among the sources.
purpose: Detect large wildlife near the roadway and warn approaching drivers in real time to reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions. The measured driver slowdown was the intended response.
system: Thermal-camera wildlife detection with AI video analytics triggering dynamic message signs (cameras and software by Crosstek)
developer: Crosstek (cameras and detection software); system integration and evaluation by Virginia Tech Transportation Institute
deployer: Virginia Department of Transportation with Virginia Tech Transportation Institute
location: Route 460 (Corridor Q) near Grundy, Buchanan County, Virginia, USA
domain: Road safety and wildlife-vehicle collision prevention
taxonomy_note: The documented effect is slower driving at warning signs; collisions avoided are not established.

ratings.reason: No individual driver or crash outcome is documented.
VDOT obtained a measured driver response (3 mph average slowdown) and 97 percent detection accuracy from a pilot, but no crash reduction.
One 750-meter test section; the report states that prevention of collisions or fatalities was not established.

ai_role.statement: AI analysis of thermal camera feeds was the trigger for the warning signs. The 3 mph slowdown is measured at signs activated by those detections, so the driver response is attributable to the detection chain. Whether any collision was prevented is explicitly not established. The results come from VTTI's own release as reproduced by Bioengineer.org, plus a WCYB launch report. No vendor (Crosstek) document and no VDOT document are among the sources.
